subject: Post-demo: latency vs concurrency — capacity decisioning for FastRetail
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: latency vs concurrency — capacity decisioning for FastRetail

Maya — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the Dedicated path cleanly.

Recap (what we heard)
- Peak concurrency pattern: spiky web inference during promotions, baseline steady state between spikes.
- Target peak TPS you mentioned: ~200 concurrent inference TPS at 95th percentile.
- Token mix: ~80% short (<100 tokens), ~20% long (200–512 tokens).
- Compliance: preference for private VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS.
- Priority: low-latency for customer-facing flows; procurement needs price comparison H100 vs A100.

Open questions / asks (quick)
1) Can you confirm whether the 200 TPS is sustained per minute or burst-per-second? That changes concurrency by ~3–5x.
2) What is the acceptable p95 latency for production? You mentioned 'snappy' — can we set a number (e.g., <=120ms p95)?
3) Any throughput/QoS expectations for batch background jobs (async reranking) vs real-time paths?
4) Will FastRetail require on-premise appliance or is VPC-only acceptable for the first phase?

Proposed next steps
- Please fill the attached capacity_workbook_fr3472.xlsx and drop the network diagram (we included a blank VPC template).
- We’ll run a quick ops estimate and come back with two concrete configs: H100-focused reserved pool and a cost-optimized A100 mix.
- Internal: Ben and Karthik will validate concurrency math and provide a rough latency/throughput sketch.
- Goal: get a sizing + high-level price delta by EOD Friday.

Attachments: capacity_workbook_fr3472.xlsx, network_diagram_vpc_fastretail.pdf (blank VPC sketch)

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Ben has validated the concurrency assumptions.

—
Sean Gallagher

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@fastretail.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency vs concurrency — capacity decisioning for FastRetail

Thanks Sean — great summary. A few clarifications below (quoting your bullets):

> Peak concurrency pattern: spiky web inference during promotions, baseline steady state between spikes.
This is correct — spikes typically come in short 30–90s bursts tied to email pushes or homepage drops.

> Target peak TPS you mentioned: ~200 concurrent inference TPS at 95th percentile.
We use TPS loosely — for clarity: we mean ~200 complete requests/sec sustained over a 1–2 minute window during peak.

> Token mix: ~80% short (<100 tokens), ~20% long (200–512 tokens).
Correct. Most user prompts are short; a small set of admin queries are longer.

> Compliance: preference for private VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS.
We will require customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for the pilot. On-prem hardware is not required for phase 1.

Latency target: Our product owners want p95 <= 120ms for the user-facing path. If that can’t be achieved with the A100 mix at our TPS, we’ll consider H100.

Pricing ask: Please provide a rough delta between an 8x A100 reserved pool vs 8x H100 reserved pool and a stepped option (4x H100 + 8x A100) — include both RU/month and committed monthly spend.

Procurement timeline: we need a vendor/architecture decision by 09/30 to hit Q4 launch windows.

Thanks — attaching a short internal networking note.

—
Maya Singh
Director of Platform Engineering, FastRetail
maya.singh@fastretail.com | +1 (212) 555-0186

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>

Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency vs concurrency — capacity decisioning for FastRetail

Maya — perfect, that helps a lot. Based on the clarified 200 RPS (1–2 minute sustained windows) and the token mix, high-level notes below:

Rough ops sketch (very conservative)
- H100 x8 reserved pool assumption: targets ~220 RPS with headroom when using ~2–3 concurrent model shards, expected p95 ~80–110ms given our current kernel/kv-cache stacking for short tokens.
- A100 x8 reserved pool assumption: targets ~150–160 RPS with p95 ~140–180ms at that RPS depending on batching; would be inside target for lower sustained traffic but risk overshoots during spikes.
- Hybrid (4x H100 + 8x A100): cost-effective middle ground — route latency-critical requests to H100 pool; background/bulk requests to A100s.

Notes on SLOs & routing
- We can implement smart routing (latency-first policy) to send p95-sensitive requests to the H100 pool and fallback to A100 when H100 is saturated.
- Prefix/KV caching for your short-token majority will materially reduce tail latency and token cost — we’ll include cache hit-rate guidance in the workbook.

Immediate next steps
1) Ben & Karthik: can you validate the conservative throughput numbers above and add a quantified concurrency-to-latency line for both H100/A100?
2) Maya: if you can confirm p95 <=120ms as the SLA target we’ll size the canary H100 capacity accordingly.
3) I’ll add a pricing delta sheet and schedule a 30-min deep-dive Friday 10am PT (if that works).

Related links: pricing sketch (internal) — https://drive.google.com/open?id=capacity_workbook_fr_3472

Thanks — I’ll queue the Friday slot and drop the workbook with a filled sample.

—
